text:
Samuel Ersson played 143 games for Philadelphia. Tonight he starts against them for the first time, in a Senators net that Linus Ullmark has made very hard to get into. Ersson's numbers this year (.884, -1.2 goals saved above expected in 10 games) are a long way from Ullmark's, but a year after finishing at -17.8 they are an improvement, and the team in front of him is rolling.

Ottawa has won three straight and is 4-0-1 in five, with 59% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) in the three wins and 53% at five on five all season. Tuesday's 2-1 win in Winnipeg ended the Jets' six-game streak and had the best story of the week: Tyler Boucher, the 10th pick in 2021, scored in his NHL debut, with his dad Brian watching. Graeme Nichols noted he joins Carter Yakemchuk as the only Ottawa first-rounders to score in a debut with the club. Viggo Björck got his first too. William Eklund is on injured reserve until about Jan. 5, so Tim Stützle has moved beside Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund. Our simulations have Ottawa at an 89% playoff chance.

Philadelphia's story is mostly off the ice. Matvei Michkov is the most written-about Flyer by a distance, with headlines asking whether he stays the season and Rick Tocchet acknowledging the noise is there. Michkov's reply has been a five-game point streak. Travis Konecny, pointless in four on 2.7 expected goals, spoke to the Ottawa beats today about his season and the reports around him, per Charlie O'Connor. The Flyers went 3-1-1 in five with 57% of the chances, a real change from 44% at five on five over the season, and they've finished 11.2 goals below what their chances usually produce.

Joseph Woll starts again after winning three straight (+4.4 saves above expected this year). These teams split two October meetings. Our numbers have Ottawa ahead in expected goals, 3.18 to 2.67, and Ottawa-born Oliver Bonk plays at home for the visitors.
headline: Samuel Ersson meets the Flyers from the other end
